summary: Client-side transform strips leading whitespace and causes resume offset misalignment for SSE/WebSocket streams
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running chat responses occasionally arrive missing a trailing JSON closing token after a reconnect. The customer uses the Redwood Node SDK with a client-side TransformStream that sanitizes chunks by trimming leading whitespace. Impact: customer application parses stream partially, ends up with duplicated midstream fragments after resume and a missing final '}' so JSON.parse on assembled response throws. Not a universal failure—only happens when a short network hiccup triggers a resume and the first resumed chunk contains leading whitespace that the client transform removes.

Observed behavior: server logs show stream resumed at offset N and sent a fragment beginning with a space/newline sequence. Client-side sanitizer removed the leading whitespace, causing the JSON boundary marker (e.g. '\n  "choices"') to merge into the previous token; client treats fragment as malformed and drops it. Server thinks offset advanced and continues; when final ']' or '}' is sent it is associated with a different byte offset and the client never sees a complete final object.

Expected behavior: resume tokens and chunk prefixes must be preserved end-to-end; client-side transforms should not remove bytes used by the resume protocol, or resume protocol should be resilient to downstream trimming.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Redwood Node SDK v2.4.1 with a TransformStream plugin that trims leading whitespace from each event chunk.
2) Initiate a long streaming completion (approx 10k tokens simulated).
3) During generation, induce a short TCP loss (e.g., disable wifi for 0.8–1.5s) to trigger reconnect/resume.
4) Observe client assembled JSON object missing trailing bracket and server logs showing resume accepted and continued from offset that no longer matches client buffer.
logs:

[api-gateway] 2026-03-10T15:21:08Z resume_request key=chatterly-cust:stream-77 offset=125432 accept=true
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T15:21:08Z resume_send offset=125432 bytes=1024 chunk_start='\n  "choices"'
[client] node-sdk v2.4.1 transform-sanitizer trimmed_chunk='"choices"' (leading newline removed)
[customer-app] parser error: Unexpected end of JSON input assembling chunks 0..X
workaround: Disable client-side trimming on streaming pipeline or upgrade to SDK patch that marks resume-sensitive bytes as protected (temporary recommendation: remove leading-whitespace sanitizer). Customer unblocked after disabling sanitizer.\n
resolution: Under investigation. Engineering (serving-runtime) to add guardrails so resume markers are emitted without leading whitespace, and SDK team to add option to bypass client transforms for resume metadata. Patch PR created for SDK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/742 (draft).

Client transform trims them and the first JSON token is merged into previous buffer. Attaching pcap to engineer thread.

2026-03-11 09:23 - Priya Singh (Client SDK): Drafted change to annotate resume frames with a magic prefix 'r:' that client transforms will skip when present. PR created as draft (see related_github_prs). Needs decision if introducing protocol prefix is acceptable for backward compatibility.
